title: River, forest, ridge
standfirst: The quietest way into the high Himalaya, and the easiest to pair with the plain.

blocks.heading: Rishikesh at the start, never at the end
paras: The river town is busy, bright and worth two nights, and it is the wrong note to end a week on.
We start there and move upstream, into forest and then into the ridges, so the trip gets quieter as it goes.

blocks.heading: Leopard and bird country
blocks.caption: A naturalist for the forest days.
paras: The forests here hold leopard, bear and some of the best birding in northern India, and almost all of it is missed without a naturalist.
We keep the same one across the stay, which matters more here than in the big parks.

blocks.heading: The high meadows
blocks.caption: Open for a few weeks in summer, and then gone.
paras: The alpine meadows above the treeline flower for a short window and are genuinely spectacular.
The window is narrow and weather-dependent, so we set those dates first and build the rest around them.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: April to June and September to November. The high meadows open briefly in summer.

items.q: Is it suitable for a first Himalayan trip?
a: Yes. Altitudes are moderate, roads are reasonable and nothing is physically demanding unless chosen.
Easily, with Delhi or with a tiger park on the same side of the country.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
